source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.section: The Influence of Position with Regard to the Sun
source_locator.short_quote: The planets, when matutine, and from their first emerging until they arrive at their first station, are chiefly productive of moisture

calculation_dependencies: superior-planet position relative to the Sun
normalized_rule: For a matutine superior planet from first emergence through first station, classify its quality as chiefly moisture-producing.
synthesis_notes: This is a position-conditioned traditional quality, not a modern astronomical measurement or natal outcome.
review_notes: The source's four superior-planet intervals are separate rules. Footnote 32's editorial discussion is not used to expand the rule to Venus or Mercury.
transmission_notes: The interval and quality are in the Ashmand/Proclus main text. The source's scope is the Moon and three superior planets; editorial station definitions are not silently added as main-text rules.
